item.title: C Language sizeof(char) Result: Why is it Always 1 Byte?
item.description:
“C Language sizeof(char) Result: Why is it Always 1 Byte?”

A recurring point of discussion in C and C++ programming involves the result returned by the sizeof operator when applied to the char type. What is the definitive size of a char, and why is the result consistently reported as 1, even on systems where memory addressing seems different?

The C99 Standard Stipulation for sizeof(char)

According to the C99 standard, specifically section 6.5.3.4, when the sizeof operator acts upon an operand of type char (or its qualified versions like signed char or unsigned char), the result is explicitly defined as 1.
